headline: Optimal transport and graph models infer cell-state transitions and signalling in tissue
label: Spatial Omics Quantitative Inference
summary: Methods now couple spatial, lineage and signalling information to infer transitions and communication, as in Niche-FATE, RegArch, mirCCC and the post-pneumonectomy lung atlas.
synthesis: The common thread is quantitative inference of cell-state dynamics and communication from single-cell data augmented with spatial, temporal, lineage or regulatory context. Niche-FATE uses optimal transport over expression, spatial neighbourhoods and ligand-receptor signalling; Tumor2Line applies unbalanced optimal transport to align tumor and cell-line populations. ChronoClone groups clones into metaclones by time-resolved state composition, RegArch reconstructs ancestral and terminal regulatory networks, and mirCCC infers miRNA-mediated communication via target repression. Global Tumor Time provides a continuous cross-patient measure of malignant progression in lung adenocarcinoma. The rat post-pneumonectomy lung atlas adds a spatial connectomic framework using Xenium and NICHES. The heart organoid atlas and the colon cancer architecture study address different questions, so the shared element is context-aware inference rather than a single algorithm.
